name: Arduino Pro Mini
summary: The minimal ATmega328 board with no USB chip, in 5 V/16 MHz and 3.3 V/8 MHz versions, designed by SparkFun for permanent installs.

clock.value: 16 MHz (5 V version) or 8 MHz (3.3 V version)

usb.value: None; program through a 6-pin FTDI-style serial adapter

gotchas.title: Pick the right clock in the IDE
gotchas.text: Selecting 16 MHz for a 3.3 V/8 MHz board (or the reverse) uploads fine but runs every timing at the wrong speed and breaks serial.

power.note: With no USB chip and a small regulator, a Pro Mini with its power LED and regulator removed can sleep at microamps, which makes it a classic for battery sensors.

editorial.history: Designed by SparkFun, the Pro Mini stripped the Arduino down to the microcontroller, a regulator and a crystal for builds where USB would only waste space and power.
editorial.today: Still widely cloned and a strong choice for coin-cell or AA-powered sensor nodes.
